The structure of K3In crystallizes in the orthorhombic space group Amm2 (No. 38), with a unit cell containing eight atoms—six K and two In—distributed over four independent Wyckoff orbits. Geometry-derived analysis shows In centers with a close-packed-like local arrangement of 12 geometric neighbors, while K centers exhibit 12- and 13-neighbor environments, with the latter forming a 13-vertex coordination polyhedron. The periodic neighbor graph is three-dimensional and connected across all eight sites. Validated polyhedron-sharing contacts include corner, edge, and face sharing among the K-centered 12- and 13-vertex polyhedra, and corner and edge sharing between In- and K-centered polyhedra.
